scope: The theorem controls the first Segre multiplicity at the generic kernel vertex and, only for a zero-dimensional vertex, an affine-degree lower bound. It does not determine later Segre degrees, singular essential tops, or transport under cotangent/Schur lifts.

theorem.input: degree-m gradient compactification in P^n; top potential depends on r<n essential variables and is smooth in P^(r-1)
theorem.non_socle_corollary: if n-r=1 and s is nonzero outside Soc(B), delta>=2*(m-q)
theorem.unit_penultimate_law: if h_m restricts nontrivially to the kernel vertex, sigma_(r+1)=m^r
